v.why: When node2->3 is absent, the direct 0->3 conv supplies a much larger share of the output's capacity, so adding it helps more.
A residual input->output shortcut mainly helps when deep conv paths exist; in skip/pool/empty cells it adds little.
With edge 4 already removed, deleting edge 5 leaves only the 0->3 path, removing all intermediate computation.
Without the 0->3 edge, removing 2->3 removes a major or the only path to the output and loses the shortcut-less network's main capacity.
Replacing none on 0->1 reactivates node 1 and its downstream edges, a bigger gain than swapping one existing op for another.
Filling a missing 0->2 edge adds a new path rather than just changing an op, giving a larger improvement.
When 0->2 is missing, node 2 depends solely on edge 2, so making it a strong conv matters much more.
If 1->2 is absent, edge 4 is node 1's only route to the output, so removing it effectively discards the 0->1 conv.
Removing the input->output skip from deep conv cells hurts optimization more than removing a redundant parallel conv.
In parameter-free pool-dominated cells, adding the first learnable 3x3 conv near the output yields a far larger accuracy jump than in conv-rich cells.
